commit_message:
Reuse c->argv after command execution to reduce memory allocation overhead (#13521)

inspred by https://github.com/redis/redis/pull/12730

Before this PR, we allocate new memory to store the user command
arguments, however, if the size of the current `c->argv` is larger than
the current command, we can reuse the previously allocated argv to avoid
allocating new memory for the current command.
And we will free `c->argv` in client cron when the client is idle for 2
seconds.

---------

Co-authored-by: Ozan Tezcan <ozantezcan@gmail.com>

findings.title: clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle frees argv while client is mid-parse, leading to later NULL deref/crash
findings.message:
clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle() frees c->argv and resets c->argv_len to 0 whenever `c->argc == 0` and the client has been idle for more than 2 seconds. However, `c->argc == 0` does not mean the client is not in the middle of receiving a command: if the client has sent a partial multibulk request (e.g. only the `*3
$3
SET
` header), `c->multibulklen` is non-zero while `c->argc` is still 0, because no argv elements have been parsed yet. The idle check only guards on `!c->argv || c->argc`, so it does not exclude this in-the-middle-of-parsing state, and the cron job frees argv (setting it to NULL) and sets argv_len to 0 out from under the client. When the client later sends the rest of the command and processMultibulkBuffer() resumes parsing, it computes the new argv size as `min(c->argv_len*2, c->argc+c->multibulklen)` which evaluates to `min(0, multibulklen)` = 0 (since argv_len is 0), so it calls zrealloc(NULL, 0), which can return NULL. c->argv is then left NULL while argc/multibulklen indicate more arguments are expected, and subsequent writes to c->argv[c->argc] dereference a NULL pointer, crashing the server.
findings.suggestion: Guard clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle so it never frees argv while the client is still in the middle of parsing a command, by also checking c->multibulklen (and ensuring argv_len tracking stays consistent elsewhere, e.g. in replaceClientCommandVector). Additionally, add a defensive assertion in processMultibulkBuffer that argv_len is non-zero before growing argv, to fail loudly instead of silently producing a NULL argv.

ground_truth.root_cause: Missing/incorrect idle-check condition: the function used to decide whether it's safe to free a client's argv only considered c->argc, not c->multibulklen, so it incorrectly treated a client that is mid-command-parse (multibulk header received but args pending) as idle/safe-to-free. This is compounded by replaceClientCommandVector() not keeping c->argv_len in sync with c->argc, which the companion fix also addresses.
